subject.title: message_tool_only: one-shot delivery reminder loses to recency over long tool chains, turns end in withheld finals

question: For long `message_tool_only` turns that end with a plain private final, should OpenClaw add periodic in-turn delivery reminders, bounded withheld-final recovery, or both?
rationale: The code shows a one-shot hint and warning-only suppression path, but choosing reminder refresh versus recovery affects prompt traffic, duplicate-delivery risk, queue semantics, and the documented privacy contract.

options.title: Combine Reminder And Recovery
options.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and a one-shot recovery path for substantive private finals, coordinated with the stranded-final recovery PR.

options.title: Recovery Only
options.body: Rely on the stranded-final recovery path to repair missed finals after the model fails, without increasing prompt traffic during long tool chains.

options.title: Reminder Only
options.body: Refresh the delivery instruction during long turns but leave withheld-final retry or diagnostics to separate recovery work.

recommendation.title: Combine Reminder And Recovery
recommendation.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and a one-shot recovery path for substantive private finals, coordinated with the stranded-final recovery PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses core delivery privacy, prompt-context behavior, and active recovery work, and the current integration history gives this the clearest routing signal.
